## 2026-09-01 21:48 UTC-05:00 · round-close · search+corpus
Searching the liver used to hand you Meat & Animal Foods. It now opens a Liver Health topic with 28 answers, and asking how to look after your liver heroes the real answer.
  ↳ A person typing "liver health" into this app was being shown red meat. That is now a Liver Health topic carrying 28 answers, and the common questions - how do I take care of my liver, which foods and nutrients support it, can a damaged liver heal - each hero the claim that actually answers them rather than dumping the reader on a page. THE DEFECT, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. Driving the live resolver on the built bundle, 12 of 20 liver queries resolved to the `meat` entity: it carried the bare synonym "liver" for organ meat and no liver-organ entity existed to outrank it. Two landed somewhere with no liver content at all - "signs of liver problems" heroed "What are the signs of too much calcium?", and "liver damage from alcohol" heroed a resveratrol high-fat-diet claim. THE FIX. A new `liver` entity, type topic, `hub: true` - the aggregation shape already used by muscle_strength, veganism and healthy_foods, where claims attach through `also_about` rather than `subject`, so nothing was re-homed and no existing page lost a claim. `intro_claim` is the British-Liver-Trust "over 500 functions" claim, so the page ledes on what the organ actually does. The bare token came off `meat`, which keeps "organ meats" and gained "beef liver" and "chicken liver" so the FOOD sense still resolves to the food entity. THE CORPUS WORK. All 230 claims whose text or quote mentions the liver, hepatic tissue, cirrhosis, jaundice or bile were triaged against one rubric - does this teach a reader about the human liver as an ORGAN: 11 CORE, 84 supporting, 14 gallbladder-only, 121 rejected. The rejects are mostly the very confusion the topic exists to fix: eating liver as food, "liver spots" (which are skin), and the liver inside a passing list of organs. 17 new claims were then mined across six books and sealed (knowledge_version 492, then 493 after the corrections; 2,617 claims). Two of them are cross-book syntheses answering the owner's own two questions: "Which foods and nutrients support a healthy liver?" - anchored on Wallach's dosed liver-disease protocol (vitamin C to bowel tolerance, vitamin A 10,000-300,000 IU as beta carotene, B-complex 100 mg t.i.d., selenium 500-1,000 mcg/day, B12 1,000 mcg/day, folic acid 15-25 mg/day, EFAs from salmon and flaxseed oil 1 gm t.i.d., milk thistle, and fried foods and margarine out) - and "How do I improve my liver health and reverse liver damage?". An adversarial auditor cut four sentences from those two before they were authored; both defects were the same class, an exclusivity claim scoped to one book and silently inflated to corpus scope, and both contradicted their own claim's text. TEN GATE REDS, ALL REAL. Sealing turned the board from 113/113 to 103/113, and every one of the ten was a genuine defect this round had introduced or exposed. The dose kind on the protocol claim was fanning one shared budget across six essentials; two claims mapped conditions their own quotes never named; one new claim shared its entire span with an existing one; the topic had no authored lede; "cholangitis" had no glossary entry; and ten claims were front-faced from books not in the verification ledger. WHAT THE OWNER CAUGHT, AND IT MATTERS MOST. He asked whether the relayed sources - the 2004 NIAAA alcohol report, the British Liver Trust, the cadmium attribution - were ones Wallach ENDORSES rather than argues against. On alcohol he does not. The quote stopped at the report's findings; three sentences later Wallach rejects the benefit half outright, saying the "benefits of alcohol" are really the benefits of the phytonutrients in the drink rather than the alcohol itself. The claim was passing that off as neutral reporting. The quote was extended from 426 to 975 characters so it carries his pushback, and the answer now says plainly which half he lets stand and which he rejects. The other two check out: the Liver Trust figure sits inside his own argument, and the cadmium passage is his own case against cadmium. TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THEY WILL RECUR OTHERWISE.   1. I told him no page image existed for Rare Earths Table 12-2 and that the claim therefore could      not be checked. That was false. My search piped through `head -25`, the repository's own USDA      PDFs filled all 25 lines, and I reported the clipped output as a fact about the world - having      also left *.png out of the pattern, which hid 753 page images. Every page of all seven books has      an image source on this machine. Rendered via PyMuPDF (poppler is not installed, so the Read      tool cannot open a PDF here), printed page 463 reads "Liver cirrhosis | Selenium, Copper,      Sulfur" on one baseline. Nothing was mis-claimed; confidence went medium to high and the page      number is recorded. The same clipping error then produced a second false alarm - a "mid-sentence      cutoff" that was my print truncating at 260 characters, not the stored verbatim.   2. Fixing the routing, I loaded the new entity's synonym list with full QUESTION phrasings ("how do      I keep my liver healthy"). resolveQuery step 1 short-circuits a whole-query synonym match      straight to mode 'entity', so every real question opened the page instead of ranking an answer -      precisely the laziness he had told me to avoid. Synonyms are now NAMES only; the three claims      that answer the common questions carry explicit intent topics; and genuinely BROAD queries      ("what damages the liver", "signs of liver problems") are deliberately kept on the page, because      no single claim is the honest answer to those. SOURCE PURIFICATION. Seven OCR defects inside newly front-faced spans were fixed at the SOURCE rather than patched in the quote: "in gen-/eral" and "pan-/creatitis" in Hell's Kitchen, and "Gallblad-/der", "choles-/terol", "barom-/eter", "ofconnective" and "GGT(gamma" in Let's Play Doctor. A new lets-play-doctor purity spec carries the audit trail; the Hell's Kitchen entries were applied out-of-band because that spec is apply-once and already baked into the text, following the precedent the immortality spec records. resnap reported 0 broken, and 514 draft claims were synced shard to draft before sealing - the seal-order trap that has cost this project four sessions. ONE GATE REFINED, MEASURED FIRST. verbatim_audit.norm turned an apostrophe into a space, so a book printing "Reye's syndrome" could never match the catalogue's "Reyes Syndrome". It now drops the apostrophe. This was measured before it was changed: 2 violations resolved - one of them pre-existing, erbs_palsy - and 0 created. That is a refinement, not a bypass. VERIFICATION. Board 112/113 with only web_build_not_stale outstanding, which this round-close then clears. A new render_probe_liver_routing pins 17 routing expectations plus the rendered page count, and it drives the real UI: it types "liver health" into the app and asserts the hero reads Liver Health with 28 answers, because a topic that resolves but renders empty is exactly the bug reported. Nine claims were whole-verbatim verified against rendered page images and added to claims_verified, now 813; PDF-text-layer agreement was used only to locate pages and is deliberately not counted as verification, per that ledger's own standard. DEFERRED, AND HIS TO RULE ON. The two synthesis claims draw on 18 and 13 further passages whose sentence-level trace lives only in temporary/liver/synthesis-provenance.json - the schema carries one verbatim per claim and has no home for the rest, so sealing them as they stand loses that trace. The options are to keep them and move the list somewhere permanent, trim each answer back to what its own quote supports, or split each into smaller claims that carry their own quotes. `cirrhosis` and `liver_cirrhosis` remain two slugs for one disease at his instruction. Ten liver questions a real reader would ask still have no Wallach answer at all - fatty-liver dosing, statins, sugar, Wilson's disease - and under the source rule they stay honest gaps. Uploading dist-web/ to SiteGround is his act; render_probe_live_host is the instrument for the host and says nothing until he has.
